name: Mui Ne
provinceNote: Vietnam Tourism’s coast page now places this shore in Lam Dong. The food page and Decision 1772/QĐ-TTg still say Binh Thuan. Vietnamese Wikipedia dates the merger to Resolution 202/2025/QH15 of 12 Jun 2025, and the new Mui Ne ward to Resolution 1671/NQ-UBTVQH15 of 16 Jun 2025, joining the old Ham Tien ward, the old Mui Ne ward, and Thien Nghiep. English Wikipedia prints about 25,000 people, and 24,275 in 1999 on 35.41 km², for the older ward. The merged ward is 50,166 people on 31 Dec 2024 across 118.59 km². Both counts stay.
dotReason: Worth it if you are already nearby
summary: You come for a kite on wet sand, with a low scrub ridge as the only dune on the skyline. Sleep on the Ham Tien strip, the beach English Wikipedia calls Rang and foreigners call Mui Ne Beach, west of the fishing ward. Red dunes are the sunset ride. Bàu Trắng is the dawn ride. Phan Thiet is the city on the way in.
timeNeeded: A beach day, plus the dune dawn
fee: No single town ticket. The sand is not given a ticket.
getThere: About four hours by road from Ho Chi Minh City. The train ends at Phan Thiet.
seoTitle: Mui Ne travel guide — kite sand, the dunes, sea wall
seoDescription: Sleep on the Ham Tien sand for the kite and the wind. Red dunes are about 22 km from Phan Thiet. White dunes are a 25 km drive or a short ride from the strip.
intro: The frame is the beach. Wet sand in front, a yellow-and-black kite in the surf, the sea behind it, and a low scrub ridge under the sky. That ridge is the dune, and it is only a band on the horizon. Sleep on the Ham Tien sand if the wind is the reason you came. English Wikipedia calls that built beach Rang, in Ham Tien, and says foreigners call it Mui Ne Beach. The fishing ward, with Ganh and Suoi Nuoc, sits farther along the bay. Do not use one name for both.

Give the morning to the harbor if you are not leaving for the white dunes. Vietnam Tourism says the boats unload just after dawn, then cards and coffee once the catch is on the sand. A first kite lesson fits the gentler morning wind on that same must-do page. The adventure page puts the stronger thermal wind at 11:00–16:00 and the kite season at October to April, with IKO instructors on the main beach strip. The sports page says the breeze is year-round. The coast page says November to April. All of those stay. A lesson fee is Check on arrival.

The red dunes are the late ride. Vietnam Tourism calls them just outside town and sends you at sunset to walk the orange slope and sandboard. The 2019 ministry workshop puts Đồi cát bay in Mui Ne ward, Phan Thiet, about 22 km from the city center, a field of about 36.8 ha. Those origins are not the same sentence. The white field is Bàu Trắng, in Hoa Thang, the symbol Decision 1772 names for the national tourism zone. The must-do page prints a 25 km drive. The adventure page prints a short drive from the main beach strip, steep 30-metre dunes, a lotus lake, and a visit at 5:00–7:00. Set the alarm for 4:30 if an ATV at sunrise is the plan. Midday sand on that field is scorching. Both distances stay. Minutes from a resort gate, and both dune fees, are Check on arrival.

Dinner is the sea wall by the fishing village, the grills Vietnam Tourism calls bo ke. You pick from the tanks: fresh oysters, lemongrass clams, garlic scallops, grilled prawns, crispy fish, and chili stuffed squid, with beer. Nguyễn Đình Chiểu is the restaurant road from the center of Mui Ne toward the village, and Tuyên Quang is the other street Vietnam Tourism’s Mui Ne food page names. On the way in from Phan Thiet, the Po Sah Inu towers stand on Ba Nai Hill in Phu Hai, about 7 km northeast of the city center. The catalogues print 7,000–15,000 VND and do not split adult and child. Hours are 7:00–17:00 on two catalogues and 7:00–18:00 on the third. Between the strip and the dunes, the fairy stream is a shallow walk: Suối Tiên on one Vietnam Tourism feature and Suối Hồng on the coast page. Take your shoes off. It is ankle-deep, not a canyon.
gettingAround: The strip is a road, not a grid you walk. Vietnam Tourism names a motorbike for the dunes and the coast. Vietnamese Wikipedia names Nguyễn Đình Chiểu (ĐT 706) and Võ Nguyên Giáp (ĐT 706B) as the two roads that tie Mui Ne to Phan Thiet. Decision 1772 names Vo Nguyen Giap and provincial roads 715, 716, and 716B along the north edge of the tourism zone. Taxi and bicycle fares are Check on arrival.

From Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam Tourism prints about four hours by road for this coast, and a four-hour taxi, bus, or car ride to Phan Thiet. The same publisher prints Mui Ne at four hours and Phan Thiet at four hours with Mui Ne 25 km farther. Vietnamese Wikipedia prints about 22 km from Phan Thiet ward to Mui Ne. The 2019 ministry note prints about 22 km from the city center to the flying dunes. 25 km and 22 km both stay. Minutes from Phan Thiet station to the strip are Check on arrival.

The train ends at Phan Thiet station, not in the fishing ward. Two Vietnam Railways notices disagree. The 4 Jul 2026 sale notice: from 11 Sep 2026 through 30 Dec 2026, SPT2 and SPT1 are on sale Friday, Saturday, and Sunday only. SPT2 leaves Saigon at 6:45 and reaches Phan Thiet at 10:42. SPT1 leaves Phan Thiet at 13:30 and reaches Saigon at 17:46. The 11 Sep 2023 notice: SPT2 leaves Saigon at 6:45 and reaches Phan Thiet at 10:40. SPT1 leaves Phan Thiet at 13:10 and reaches Saigon at 17:35. Fares are Check on arrival. Weekday trains outside that 2026 window are Check on arrival. Vietnam Tourism also names Mui Ne as an open-tour stop. The operator and the clock are Check on arrival.

No civil passenger airport is open on this coast. The Phu Quy page says there is no airport in Phan Thiet, so the flight is to Ho Chi Minh City, Nha Trang, or Da Lat, then a bus or a train. The Civil Aviation Authority records the civil-terminal groundbreaking at Phan Thiet on 27 Apr 2026. The military side was already operating. A passenger opening date is Check on arrival. Decision 1772, written in 2018, names Tan Son Nhat and Cam Ranh as the air links, and a Phan Thiet airport only after 2025. Minutes from those airports to the strip are Check on arrival.

stayAreas.name: Ham Tien sand
stayAreas.summary: Medium and small resorts sit in the Mui Ne–Ham Tien sea zone, about 340 ha on the 2018 plan. Smaller rooms are named for the ward centers and the fishing village.

eat: Dinner is the sea wall by the fishing village. The local list starts with lẩu thả, mực một nắng, and the grill you pick from the tanks. Nguyễn Đình Chiểu and Tuyên Quang are the restaurant roads.
Twenty-eight plates are named, from the Mui Ne food page, the sea-wall list, and the ministry’s Binh Thuan coast menu. A stall price is Check on arrival.
interestsBody: Eat on the sea wall, then along Nguyễn Đình Chiểu. The kite wind is on the Ham Tien sand. The red slope is the sunset picture. Bàu Trắng is the dawn picture.
The night the 2018 plan names sits in the Mui Ne–Ham Tien sea zone. Po Sah Inu is the Cham stop on the road in from Phan Thiet, not a sight inside the fishing ward.

interestGroups.summary: For a day on the Ham Tien sand, when the kite is why you stayed.
body: The lesson beach is the Ham Tien sand. Vietnam Tourism’s must-do page says the wind is gentler in the morning and stronger in the late afternoon. The adventure page puts the thermal wind at 11:00–16:00, October to April, and names IKO instructors. The sports page says the breeze is year-round. The coast page says November to April. A lesson fee is Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Dawn boats
paragraphs: Just after dawn, stand out of the way at the fishing-village market while the boats unload. Vietnam Tourism says cards and coffee follow once the catch is on the sand. Arrive at noon and the market the must-do page describes is already over. Minutes from a resort gate are Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Sea wall after dark
paragraphs: The evening area is the sea wall by the fishing village. You pick seafood from the tanks and eat on the wall. The must-do list names oysters, lemongrass clams, garlic scallops, grilled prawns, crispy fish, and chili stuffed squid, with beer. A closing hour was not given. Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Nguyễn Đình Chiểu
paragraphs: Nguyễn Đình Chiểu runs from the center of Mui Ne toward the fishing village, and Tuyên Quang is the other street Vietnam Tourism lines with rooms from cozy to cosmopolitan. Decision 1772 puts the night activity in the Mui Ne sea zone and does not name a second nightlife district. The hour the road goes quiet is Check on arrival.

cards.title: Wind on the strip
cards.summary: Ham Tien sand, a gentler morning lesson, and a stronger wind from 11:00 to 16:00.

interestGroups.title: The two dune fields
interestGroups.summary: For the sunset slope in the fishing ward, and the pale field at Hoa Thang before the heat.

blocks.heading: Red slope at the end of the day
paragraphs: Đồi cát bay is the orange field. Vietnam Tourism says just outside town, at sunset, for the walk and the sandboard. The 2019 ministry workshop says about 36.8 ha in Mui Ne ward, Phan Thiet, about 22 km from the city center, and says that since 2016 the field was assigned to the provincial youth outdoor center. The 22 km figure is from the city center, not from a resort gate. A ticket was not given. Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: White field and the lake
paragraphs: Bàu Trắng is in Hoa Thang, Bac Binh, inside the national tourism zone. Decision 1772 calls it the symbol of Mui Ne. Bàu Sen is named with it for protection and is not given a separate visit. The adventure page prints steep 30-metre dunes, a lotus lake, and a visit from 5:00 to 7:00. The must-do page prints a 25 km drive. The adventure page prints a short drive from the main beach strip. Both stay. The fee is Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: A shallow walk inland
paragraphs: The fairy stream sits under the Mui Ne sand hills. Vietnam Tourism’s Binh Thuan feature calls it Suối Tiên. The coast page calls it Suối Hồng and also the fairy stream. Both names stay. You take your shoes off and walk upstream in ankle-deep water, red clay and limestone on one side. A coconut at a rest stop is named. A street address, a minute count, and a ticket are Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Tower on the way in
paragraphs: Tháp Pô Sah Inư stands on Ba Nai Hill in Phu Hai, about 7 km northeast of Phan Thiet center, on the road between the city and the strip. Vietnam Tourism calls the three brick towers 1,200-year-old Hoa Lai national monuments. The main tower holds a Linga-Yoni altar. Three catalogues print 7,000–15,000 VND and do not split adult and child. Hours are 7:00–17:00 on the English catalogue and the older Binh Thuan catalogue, and 7:00–18:00 on the Vietnamese catalogue. Addresses disagree: the English intro leaves the line blank, the Vietnamese catalogue prints Km9 Nguyễn Thông, Phường Phú Thuỷ, Lâm Đồng, and the older catalogue prints Phường Phú Hài, Phan Thiết, Bình Thuận. The morning of 2 Oct 2024 was Katê at these towers. The next civil date is Check on arrival.

faqs.a: On the Ham Tien sand if the kite and the resort row are the reason you came. Decision 1772 puts medium and small resorts in the Mui Ne–Ham Tien sea zone, about 340 ha, and smaller rooms in the ward centers and the fishing village. English Wikipedia calls the built sand Rang Beach, west of the fishing ward.

faqs.q: How do you get here from Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Vietnam Tourism prints about four hours by road. The same publisher also prints Phan Thiet at four hours with Mui Ne 25 km farther. Vietnamese Wikipedia prints about 22 km from Phan Thiet ward to Mui Ne. The train ends at Phan Thiet station. From 11 Sep 2026 through 30 Dec 2026, Vietnam Railways sells SPT2 and SPT1 on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday: Saigon 6:45, Phan Thiet 10:42, and back 13:30 to 17:46. A 2023 notice prints 10:40 and a return at 13:10–17:35. Fares are Check on arrival.

The must-do page says the morning wind is gentler and the late afternoon is stronger. The adventure page puts kite winds at October to April and the beach window at 11:00–16:00. The sports page says the breeze is year-round. The coast page says November to April. A lesson fee is Check on arrival.

The red dunes are about 22 km from the Phan Thiet city center on the 2019 ministry page, and just outside town on Vietnam Tourism’s must-do page. The white dunes are a 25 km drive on that must-do page, and a short drive from the main beach strip on the adventure page. Minutes from a resort gate are Check on arrival. Be at Bàu Trắng from 5:00 to 7:00.

season.label: Dry wind months
season.note: Vietnam Tourism’s coast page calls November to April dry, sunny, and windy, the time for kites and dune slides. The adventure page puts kite winds at October to April, with the beach window at 11:00–16:00. The sports page says the breeze and the water stay warm year-round. English Wikipedia calls December to April the tourist season and prints an average of 27°C. The Binh Thuan feature prints warm sun all year and daily temperatures around 27°C. On the white dunes, go at 5:00–7:00. Midday sand is scorching.
